answer: Make each agent's reputation a costly, slowly built graph: every service interaction creates a vertex in a shared trust graph, and only vertices with a long history of verified, useful work gain weight. New identities start at zero and must earn standing through repeated, costly contributions that can't be faked in bulk, like water carving karst slowly rather than in one flood. A reputation echo from many long-lived peers then outweighs any self-attestation, so a sybil swarm spinning up thousands of fresh accounts stays powerless: it can copy words, but not years of cross-checked history.
